model.title: Choosing a local model
model.subtitle: Policy examples. The recorded chat explicitly selected Alex.

beats.title: Read the phone’s current limits
beats.detail: Automatic selection uses physical memory, Low Power Mode and thermal state. It does not benchmark the phone.
beats.code:
Example A
6 GB memory · Low Power Mode off · nominal temperature
Automatic choice: Alex (0.5B)

beats.title: Use Sam when the policy permits
beats.detail: At least 8 GB, normal power and nominal temperature select Sam. Otherwise it selects Alex. Camille (7B) is a manual option.
beats.code:
Example B
12 GB memory · Low Power Mode off · nominal temperature
Automatic choice: Sam (1.5B)
Visit summaries promote Alex to Sam; manual Camille stays selected.

beats.title: Reuse a verified download
beats.detail: If the files are missing, download pinned model assets and verify their size and SHA-256 before installation. Partial files stay in staging.
beats.code:
Verified local weights ────────────── ready
Missing weights → download → verify → install
Download is network access; inference runs locally.

beats.title: Generate inside llama.cpp
beats.detail: The runtime loads GGUF weights. Physical devices request Metal layers; Simulator uses CPU. Effort controls output budgets, not model size.
beats.code:
Standard effort: router ≤ 160 tokens · chat ≤ 512 tokens
Quick / Standard / Extended change those budgets.
Summary passes use separate fixed budgets.

chat.title: A message becomes a tool request
chat.subtitle: Architecture illustration. The recorded request actually executed list_readings.

beats.title: Build a bounded prompt
beats.detail: Combine the message with the tool list, a limited saved-record snapshot and recent conversation turns. A selected topic is only a hint.
beats.code:
Message: Show my recent blood pressure readings
Context: saved medicines, recent readings, symptoms
History: up to six recent turns
Topic: optional; it does not execute an action

beats.title: The LLM selects the intent
beats.detail: Constrained JSON names one tool. This is a model decision, rather than a keyword rule choosing which action to run.

beats.title: Check the decision against the request
beats.detail: Parse the output and validate requested actions against original input and saved identities. Unsupported write requests can be rejected or clarified.
beats.code:
LLM proposal → parse → source checks
Read tool: continue to dispatcher
Unsupported write: reject or ask for clarification
Validation is a guard, not a guarantee of medical accuracy.

beats.title: Route to the matching implementation
beats.detail: Read tools fetch saved data. Write tools open the shared review controls. A reply intent asks the model to generate ordinary conversation.
beats.code:
list_readings → filter saved records → newest ten → table
add_medication / update_medication → medicine review
capture_symptom / log_reading → shared entry editor
reply → generated conversation

voice.title: Voice uses the same conversation
voice.subtitle: Illustrated speech path. This footage does not measure audio recognition or voice quality.
sources: Harbour/DeviceServices.swift · VoiceService; Harbour/ChatView.swift · voice turns, send

beats.title: Listen on the phone
beats.detail: Voice conversation captures microphone audio and reports listening levels. Dictation only fills the composer; voice conversation continues the agent loop.
beats.code:
Microphone → Apple on-device recognizer
Language follows the app’s English / French choice.
Medication-name hints guide recognition; they are not corrections.

beats.title: Finalize recognized words
beats.detail: The on-device recognizer supplies partial text while listening. The completed turn, rather than every partial fragment, becomes the message submitted to the agent.
beats.code:
Partial recognition → finalized turn
Medication hints bias recognition toward known names.
They do not verify that a medicine was actually spoken.

beats.title: Send the finished turn as text
beats.detail: The completed utterance enters the normal chat pipeline. Model-selected tools, review screens and conversation history remain the same.
beats.code:
Finished utterance → chat message → local LLM
                 ↳ tool request or generated reply
The full-screen voice view hides text, but chat history remains.

beats.title: Speak the response locally
beats.detail: Kokoro synthesizes the response into audio chunks for playback. The voice view reflects listening, thinking and speaking states.
beats.code:
Agent response → text chunks → Kokoro → audio playback
The next listening turn continues the conversation.
Speech assets may need an initial download.

medicine.title: Intent and medicine identity are separate
medicine.subtitle: The recorded editor shows a real name suggestion. The routing example below is illustrative.

beats.title: Choose the action first
beats.detail: The local model distinguishes adding, updating, removing and asking a question. Validation then checks whether that action was actually requested.
beats.code:
Illustrative message: Update my metformin to 400 mg
Model intent: update_medication
Source checks: saved medicine identity + requested directions
Result: a review draft, not a deletion or silent overwrite

beats.title: Resolve names without guessing ingredients
beats.detail: Saved and exact database identities take precedence. Similar spellings produce candidates in the editor; the app does not silently replace the original text.
beats.code:
Typed: hydroclorothiazide
Candidate: Hydrochlorothiazide
Source: Health Canada Drug Product Database vocabulary
Candidate ≠ confirmed medicine

beats.title: Review identity and directions together
beats.detail: The existing medicine editor displays the chosen product, instructions and schedule. A proposed correction remains a draft until the user checks it.
beats.code:
Selected candidate: Hydrochlorothiazide
Check the exact product and ingredients.
Review label directions, frequency and times.
An unchecked product cannot be saved.

beats.title: Keep the user at the write boundary
beats.detail: The shared editor shows identity, instructions and schedule. The user checks the intended product and confirms before the record store changes.
beats.code:
Choose candidate → check product → review directions → Save
No confirmed selection: Save stays disabled.
These name entries are not a complete interaction database.

recording.title: Recording and transcription run together
recording.subtitle: Illustrated backend. The displayed visit uses an authored transcript and summary fixture.

beats.title: Start one recording session
beats.detail: After permissions and audio-session setup, AVAudioEngine supplies buffers. A single writer saves audio and forwards buffers to the speech session.
beats.code:
Microphone → AVAudioEngine → audio buffers
                         ├─ save .m4a locally
                         └─ feed live speech recognition
Meter updates also drive the recording display.

beats.title: Keep audio even if speech fails
beats.detail: The recorder supports background audio while locked. Live Activities report session state. If recognition is unavailable or falls behind, audio can still be retained for retry.
beats.code:
Local recording + session state
Live Activity / Dynamic Island: recording or paused
Recognition failure: retain audio + show a warning
Interrupted sessions are marked for recovery.

beats.title: Transcribe with the available Apple service
beats.detail: On iOS 26, live visits use SpeechAnalyzer and SpeechTranscriber. The older path requires on-device SFSpeechRecognizer support. Live speech receives medication hints.
beats.code:
iOS 26 live path: audio → SpeechAnalyzer → transcript
Earlier path: audio → on-device SFSpeechRecognizer
Saved audio may be transcribed again after the visit.
No cloud transcription fallback is shown here.

beats.title: Save the text as summary input
beats.detail: The saved visit retains its audio reference and transcript. An empty failed retry does not replace a previously saved transcript. Summary extraction starts from the text.
beats.code:
Saved visit
  audio reference + transcript + session warnings
                          ↓
                  summary pipeline

summary.title: Three focused passes per transcript chunk
summary.subtitle: Pipeline illustration, not an executed extraction of this demo visit. Proposals can still be missed or rejected.

beats.title: Split text into bounded chunks
beats.detail: The app groups words into chunks of at most 1,800 characters and takes a baseline of saved medications. Each chunk goes through the same three passes, sequentially.
beats.code:
Illustrative transcript
Increase amlodipine to 10 mg once daily at 8 am.
Repeat blood work in two weeks. Home readings reviewed.

Visit model: Sam when the chat selection is Alex.

beats.title: Pass 1: medication instructions
beats.detail: The prompt asks for explicit start, update or stop orders, complete directions and an exact source quote. Constrained JSON defines the output shape.
beats.code:
medicines → action + name + instructions + source quote
Example proposal: update amlodipine
Directions: 10 mg once daily at 8 am
Budget: up to 1,536 output tokens

beats.title: Pass 2: follow-ups and appointments
beats.detail: A separate prompt extracts tests, monitoring and future tasks, plus explicit appointment details. It must preserve dates and conditions without booking anything.
beats.code:
followUps: Repeat blood work in two weeks.
appointments: only explicitly supported appointment details
Each item keeps its source quote.
Budget: up to 1,024 output tokens

beats.title: Pass 3: discussion highlights
beats.detail: The final prompt extracts concise discussion points without repeating full medicine directions. This is not a second model voting on or repairing the earlier passes.
beats.code:
highlights: Home readings reviewed.
Preserve negation, uncertainty and numbers.
Keep supporting source quotes.
Budget: up to 768 output tokens

beats.title: Validate the proposals and combine them
beats.detail: Parsing checks quotes and source-supported fields, including medication instructions and action context. Supported results merge across passes and chunks; omitted facts are not invented by a recovery step.
beats.code:
Candidates → source checks → supported summary fields
Unknown medication identity can require manual review.
No guaranteed completeness: extraction can still miss an instruction.
Summary saves with transcript + medication baseline.

beats.title: Review before changing medication records
beats.detail: Saving a summary does not apply its medication proposals. The review checks selected changes and acknowledgement; a changed medication baseline blocks stale application.
beats.code:
Summary saved → proposed changes remain unapplied
Review → select changes → confirm instructions → Save
Changed baseline / conflicting changes: stop and review again
